result.summary: Do not implement as written: the expanded protection set breaks supported symlinked-core uninstalls and strands credentials.

findings.title: Distinguish chain-link protection from shelf-subtree protection
findings.body: For a supported layout such as `<core> -> /data/wienerdog`, X17(1a) puts `/data/wienerdog` into the protected set. X18 then preserves every deletion target beneath it, including `app`, `logs`, and `secrets`, even when both shelves are absent. A read-only model of the prescribed containment checks confirms this. Existing symlinked-core tests require those contents to be removed. Meanwhile, `uninstall.js:424` still deletes the manifest unconditionally after the sweep, leaving credentials and installed files behind without a usable uninstall retry. This requires no concurrent mutation and falls inside the declared chain-closure scope.
findings.recommendation: Separate protected shelf subtrees from resolution-chain nodes. Protect chain nodes against removal of the node or its ancestors without protecting unrelated descendants. Add symlinked-core regressions with absent and empty shelves, asserting that ordinary mechanics and credentials are removed.

next_steps: Revise X17/X18 containment semantics and verify the existing symlinked-core uninstall expectations remain satisfiable.
